summary: Amgen's dazodalibep posted positive full Phase 3 data in Sjögren's disease, which has no FDA-approved drug; Novartis's ianalumab is the rival.
An expert wrap-up named Lilly's retatrutide the top practice-changer: knee osteoarthritis pain fell alongside up to 29% weight loss.
argenx's efgartigimod won in myositis (p=0.0011), but its Sjögren's trial was stopped in October 2026.
UCB's bimekizumab beat AbbVie's risankizumab head-to-head in psoriatic arthritis, while CAR-T lupus data shifted toward 12-month durability.

items.title: OASIZ-301 Phase 3, dazodalibep (CD40 ligand blocker) in Sjogren's disease (Amgen); ianalumab extension (Novartis)
lines: ESSDAI (EULAR Sjogren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index) change at week 48: -5.6 (every 4 weeks) and -5.2 (every 12 weeks) vs -3.8 placebo, adjusted p<0.001 and p=0.010, n=648
ESSPRI (patient-reported index) dryness domain: placebo-adjusted difference -1.17 points, adjusted p<0.001; Amgen reported no imbalance in thromboembolic events or opportunistic infections
Novartis ianalumab NEPTUNUS long-term extension (abstract LB14) presented as the competing B-cell (BAFF receptor) option; figures not reported in sources opened
Late-breaking oral LB22; Amgen notes Sjogren's disease has no FDA-approved treatment; Amgen topline results were first announced September 2026

items.title: TRIUMPH-4 retatrutide in knee osteoarthritis with obesity; TOGETHER-PsA ixekizumab plus tirzepatide (Eli Lilly)
lines: WOMAC (Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index) pain change: -4.4 to -4.5 points vs -2.4 placebo, p<0.001, n=445, 68 weeks; Plenary I
Body weight change: -26% to -29% vs -2.1% placebo in TRIUMPH-4; 80-week TRIUMPH-1-OA showed -18.6% to -28.7%
TOGETHER-PsA: week-52 ACR50 (50% improvement in American College of Rheumatology criteria) 43.7% vs 15.7% ixekizumab alone, nominal p<0.001, n=271
Janet Pope (RheumNow) ranked retatrutide number 1 practice-changer; open question whether benefit is weight loss alone or structure-modifying

items.title: ALKIVIA Phase 3, efgartigimod subcutaneous (FcRn, neonatal Fc receptor, blocker) in myositis (argenx)
lines: Week-52 Total Improvement Score 47.95 vs 32.56 placebo, difference 15.4, p=0.0011, n=175; late-breaking oral LB24
Total Improvement Score of at least 40 achieved by more patients on drug: 27.2 percentage-point difference vs placebo; separation seen from week 4
Covered immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy and dermatomyositis with steroid tapering; Pope flagged class-effect low antibody levels (hypogammaglobulinemia)
Negative: per Pope, an efgartigimod randomized trial in Sjogren's disease was stopped in October 2026; figures not reported

items.title: BE BOLD head-to-head, bimekizumab vs risankizumab in psoriatic arthritis (UCB vs AbbVie)
lines: Week-16 ACR50 49.1% bimekizumab vs 38.0% risankizumab, p=0.0058, n=553; Phase 3b, Plenary III
MDA (minimal disease activity) difference not statistically significant (figures not reported); Candida yeast infections more frequent with bimekizumab
Pope ranked it a top-6 practice-changer but noted uncertainty about which to choose when skin disease is severe

items.title: REDUCE-2 Phase 3, pozdeutinurad (URAT1, urate transporter 1, inhibitor) in gout (Sobi)
lines: Serum urate below 6 mg/dL at month 6: 69.2% (75 mg) and 56.6% (50 mg) vs 8.1% placebo, p<0.0001, n=811
Kidney stones in 1.8% or fewer of patients; late-breaking oral LB20
Pope: safety in chronic kidney disease unclear and not all patients had failed allopurinol or febuxostat, so positioning is uncertain

items.title: Lupus: obinutuzumab REGENCY kidney biopsies (Roche); afimetoran oral TLR7/8 (toll-like receptor) inhibitor Phase 2 (Beeline Medicines, no listed ticker found)
lines: Obinutuzumab: among patients without complete kidney response, 52.6% vs 8.3% placebo reached NIH (National Institutes of Health) activity index 0 at week 76; kidney B cells fell (p<0.0001)
Afimetoran: week-48 SRI-4 (SLE Responder Index-4) 64-68% across three doses vs 34.4% placebo, p<0.001, n=248
Afimetoran serious adverse events 5.9% vs 12.9% placebo; late-breaking oral LB23
AstraZeneca (AZN) anifrolumab LASER real-world study: steroid-related damage HR 0.128 and eye damage HR 0.102 vs matched controls over 4 years

items.title: CAR-T cell therapy in autoimmune disease: zola-cel (Bristol Myers Squibb), rese-cel (Cabaletta Bio), zugo-cel (CRISPR Therapeutics)
lines: Zola-cel Breakfree-1 lupus: SLEDAI-2K (SLE Disease Activity Index 2000) fell by a median 10 points at 12 months, 91% off immunosuppressants, n=34; CRS (cytokine release syndrome) mostly grade 1
Rese-cel refractory dermatomyositis: 6 of 6 patients improved and stayed off immunomodulators at one year, 5 off steroids; grade 1 CRS in 2, no neurotoxicity
Zugo-cel (off-the-shelf) systemic sclerosis: median mRSS (modified Rodnan skin score) 36 to 25.5, 4 of 6 met CRISS-25; one pulmonary embolism possibly related, n=6
ACR press office also highlighted the Phase 1 COMPARE CD19 CAR-T trial in refractory rheumatoid arthritis; figures not reported

expert_minds: Healio pre-meeting survey: CAR-T and its safety, lupus, Sjogren's disease, AI, GLP-1 drugs, long COVID and drug costs were top of mind
ACR President William Harvey: innovation and cell-based therapies like CAR-T drive the meeting; Brian Anderson's opening session focused on responsible AI
Janet Pope (RheumNow): obesity drug retatrutide is the biggest practice-changer, followed by lupus and Sjogren's trials, myositis, gout and head-to-head PsA
Alexis Ogdie (ACR year in preview): cell therapy, lupus, PsA and Sjogren's most researched in 2026; Rheumatology Advisor added an immunometabolic theme; Jack Cush noted many first-in-class mechanisms
topics: GLP-1 and incretin drugs in osteoarthritis and PsA
Lupus new mechanisms (TLR7/8, CD40L, type 1 interferon)
